problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=2\pi $ and velocity $v=4$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Position Function of a Particle Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2{e}^{2t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x={e}^{2}$ and velocity $v={e}^{2}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2{e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & ={e}^{2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & ={e}^{2(1)}+C \\ {e}^{2} & ={e}^{2}+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)={e}^{2t}.$ 

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2(1)}+K \\ {e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+K \\ K & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.
$$
